title: Musée Vision — Sculpture Wing
description: Candidate sculptures for a new wing, from the circle of the Impressionists in France (c.1830–1930). 'core' marks the headline set; 'gallery' refers to the ids in 'galleries'. 'rights' is the copyright status of the work itself (US / EU life+70). 'scan' is the best openly downloadable 3D model found as of 2026-09-23. A scan carries its own license, separate from the work's copyright. 'scan.permissive' is true only for CC0 or CC-BY, which are safe for a paid app with attribution. Triangle counts are for the source file; decimate to ~100–300k for Vision Pro.

sculptures.title: The Departure of the Volunteers of 1792 (La Marseillaise)
sculptures.notes: Precursor. 'La Marseillaise' is a nickname. Architectural relief several metres high.

scan.source: Plaster cast of the head only (damaged)

sculptures.title: Celebrities of the Juste Milieu
sculptures.medium: Unbaked clay, painted in oil (36 busts)
sculptures.notes: Caricature busts of parliamentarians, each about 12–30 cm. Could pair with Ratapoil (c.1850–51; bronzes are posthumous).

sculptures.title: Ugolino and His Sons
sculptures.notes: Plaster and bronze at the Orsay. Beware of a Scan the World record titled 'Ugolino and his Sons' that is actually by Lambeaux.

scan.source: Met's own scan of its marble (reported; download not yet confirmed)

sculptures.title: The Dance
sculptures.notes: Moved from the Opéra Garnier façade to the Louvre in 1964, then to the Orsay in 1986; Belmondo's copy stands on the façade now. Ink was thrown at it in 1869.

scan.source: Opéra Garnier façade copy, not the Orsay original (Orsay scans are NC)

sculptures.title: The Triumph of the Republic
sculptures.notes: An outdoor monument about 12 m high. Suits the Atrium or a courtyard better than a gallery room. A model is at the Petit Palais.

scan.source: The actual monument at Place de la Nation (texture removed)

sculptures.title: The Age of Bronze
sculptures.notes: So lifelike that critics accused Rodin of casting from a live model.

scan.source: Cleveland Museum of Art's own bronze cast

sculptures.title: The Thinker
sculptures.notes: Conceived at about 70 cm for The Gates of Hell. The monumental cast stood at the Panthéon from 1906.

sculptures.title: The Kiss
sculptures.notes: The State marble, carved with Jean Turcan. Other marbles are at the Tate and the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek.

scan.source: Visitor scan of the Musée Rodin marble

sculptures.title: The Gates of Hell
sculptures.notes: Never finished. The Thinker and The Kiss both started here. The first bronze was cast in 1926–28 for Philadelphia. It could anchor the room's end wall.

sculptures.title: The Burghers of Calais
sculptures.notes: A monument without a heroic pedestal. Place at floor level so visitors walk among the figures.

scan.source: Full group, cast location not stated (CC0 alternative: Cleveland's head of Pierre de Wissant)

sculptures.title: Monument to Balzac
sculptures.notes: The plaster was rejected at the 1898 Salon. Often called the start of modern sculpture.

sculptures.title: The Walking Man
sculptures.notes: A fragment presented as a finished work.

sculptures.title: After the Storm
sculptures.collection: National Museum of Women in the Arts
sculptures.notes: The plaster won a medal at the 1876 Salon. The great actress was also a sculptor.

sculptures.title: The Waltz
sculptures.notes: Edition published by Eugène Blot, 1905.

sculptures.title: The Mature Age
sculptures.notes: Read as an allegory of her break with Rodin. Hang it where it is visible from the Rodin room.

sculptures.title: The Wave
sculptures.notes: Inspired by Hokusai. Echoes the Japonisme in the Salon's paintings.

sculptures.title: Woman at Her Toilet
sculptures.notes: Height not yet confirmed.

sculptures.title: Little Dancer Aged Fourteen
sculptures.medium: Wax, silk, satin, hair (bronzes posthumous, from 1922)
sculptures.notes: The only sculpture Degas ever exhibited (1881). Label the wax as the original and the bronzes as posthumous casts.

scan.source: Met bronze cast (fan scan); lighter MFA Boston cast about 37k triangles, CC-BY

sculptures.title: Dancer Looking at the Sole of Her Right Foot
sculptures.originalTitle: Danseuse regardant la plante de son pied droit
sculptures.notes: Havemeyer 'A' set. Alternative: Horse Galloping on Right Foot (25 cm).

sculptures.title: Be in Love and You Will Be Happy
sculptures.medium: Carved and painted linden wood relief
sculptures.notes: A wall relief, so it can hang as a panel.

sculptures.title: Oviri
sculptures.notes: His largest ceramic, fired in Chaplet's kiln. RMN-Grand Palais's scan can be viewed but not downloaded.

sculptures.title: Venus Victrix
sculptures.notes: Guino is legally co-author (d. 1973), so protected in the EU until 2044. Probably public domain in the US. Optional; could be dropped.

scan.source: Scan the World, Petit Palais cast

sculptures.title: Madame X
sculptures.notes: A face barely emerging from the wax.

sculptures.title: Ecce Puer
sculptures.notes: The closest thing to Impressionism in sculpture. Italian, worked in Paris 1889–c.1920. Needs a custom model or photogrammetry.

sculptures.title: Count Robert de Montesquiou
sculptures.notes: The 'Russian Rodin'; loose, Impressionist modelling.

sculptures.title: The Mediterranean
sculptures.notes: Classical calm, set against Rodin. Permissive scans exist only for other Maillol works (La Montagne, Three Graces, Action enchaînée: percapto on Sketchfab, CC-BY).

sculptures.title: Hercules the Archer
sculptures.notes: Bourdelle was Rodin's assistant. A dynamic diagonal pose.

sculptures.title: Polar Bear
sculptures.notes: Pompon was another Rodin assistant. Smooth, simplified form; a strong centrepiece.

sculptures.title: The Back I–IV
sculptures.notes: Public domain in the EU since 2025, but probably protected in the US until about 2045–2051. Outside the Impressionist theme. Optional; could be dropped.
